title: Sarvam releases updated 105B AI model with single-GPU download
summary: Sarvam releases updated 105B AI model featuring single-GPU download capability
detailed: Sarvam has released Sarvam-105B-1711, an updated open-weight AI model aimed at customer support, voice services and business agents, alongside a smaller-format download designed for a single workstation graphics card.
The release builds on the existing Sarvam 105B base rather than introducing a separate foundation model.
Sarvam's model card says the evaluations were run by its own team, and its Indic test uses a language model to judge responses.
Sarvam puts the new model's blended inference price at $0.15 per million tokens, down from $0.44.
sentences: Sarvam has released Sarvam-105B-1711, an updated open-weight AI model aimed at customer support, voice services and business agents, alongside a smaller-format download designed for a single workstation graphics card.
The Indian AI company announced the checkpoint on 22 November.
It says the update improves instruction following, tool use and Indian-language performance over its February release, while lowering the cost of serving the model.
The release builds on the existing Sarvam 105B base rather than introducing a separate foundation model.
Its published model card describes 105 billion parameters in total, with 10.3 billion active during processing.
Sarvam has made the weights available through Hugging Face in two formats.
The BF16 version is intended for further training, while the compressed NVFP4 release is the version offered through its Token Factory service.
According to the company, that 65GB build can run on one Nvidia RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell graphics card with 96GB of memory.
The claim concerns workstation-class equipment, not a typical laptop or consumer PC.
Sarvam is pitching that option to organisations that want to run agents within their own premises rather than send documents to an outside model service.
It names banks, government departments and other sectors with sensitive data among the intended users.
The company also describes applications in its Indus Cowork product and Samvaad voice-agent service.
The latter uses a voice-focused fine-tune, rather than simply treating every published checkpoint as the same model.
Across a group of eight tests of conversational agents, Sarvam puts the new release's average at 73.9.
It reports 42.6 for the February version.
Those tests cover areas including instructions, conversation quality, tool calls and Indian languages.
The company says its internal Indic suite improved from 30.1 to 79.1.
The scores are vendor-reported results.
Sarvam's model card says the evaluations were run by its own team, and its Indic test uses a language model to judge responses.
The figures are therefore not an independent audit of performance in a bank, call centre or government office.
Sarvam has also published separate results for the higher-precision and compressed builds.
Those versions do not score identically on every task, making the format and test conditions relevant when reading the comparisons.
Sarvam puts the new model's blended inference price at $0.15 per million tokens, down from $0.44.
That blended figure combines input and output charges; it is not a flat price for every million output tokens.
The company attributes the reduction to improvements in its training and serving systems on Nvidia Blackwell hardware.
It also says continued training extended the context window to 160,000 tokens, allowing the model to work with longer material.
Sarvam's update pairs downloadable weights with a lower-cost hosted option for business agents.
The main change is a new checkpoint of its existing 105B model, with claimed gains in practical conversation tasks.
Independent deployments will be needed to show how closely those test results match everyday work.
